organization: Chemapol Bratislava / Petrimex (Czechoslovak state foreign-trade enterprise)
description: Joined the state foreign-trade company Chemapol Bratislava (renamed Petrimex in 1980) after graduating, working in its chemicals and plastics trading groups and rising to deputy head of a trading group; from 1985 he was the company's representative in Morocco, returning after the Velvet Revolution. He joined the Communist Party of Czechoslovakia in 1980.

Became managing director of Agrofert, then a newly founded Czech subsidiary of Petrimex, in January 1993 and later its 100% owner, building it into a holding of agricultural, food-processing and chemical companies, which also acquired media assets such as the MAFRA publishing house (2013). He left the company's management on joining the government in 2014 but remained owner until the shares were placed in trust funds in February 2017; he was again sole shareholder from October 2025 until the transfer to the RSVP Trust on 20 February 2026 (see companies).

Founded the ANO civic initiative in 2011, which became a political movement in 2012 with Babiš as chairman. ANO sat with the liberal ALDE/Renew Europe family until 21 June 2024; on 30 June 2024 Babiš co-announced the Patriots for Europe alliance in Vienna with Viktor Orbán (Fidesz) and Herbert Kickl (FPÖ).

role: Member of the Chamber of Deputies
organization: Chamber of Deputies of the Parliament of the Czech Republic (Poslanecká sněmovna)
description: Elected in 2013 (Prague), 2017 (Central Bohemian Region), 2021 (Ústí nad Labem Region) and 2025 (Moravian-Silesian Region). Between 2021 and 2025 he led the largest opposition group. Mandate periods as recorded in the Central Register of Declarations: 26 Oct 2013–26 Oct 2017, 21 Oct 2017–20 Oct 2021, 9 Oct 2021–8 Oct 2025, and since 4 Oct 2025.

role: First Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Finance
organization: Government of the Czech Republic (cabinet of Bohuslav Sobotka)
description: Served in the ČSSD–ANO–KDU-ČSL coalition. He introduced electronic registration of sales (EET), the VAT control statement and proposed domestic reverse charging of VAT; critics argued the measures burdened small businesses while benefiting large firms such as his own. He was dismissed on 24 May 2017 after a coalition crisis over allegations, which he denied, that he had avoided taxes in 2012 while running Agrofert.

role: Prime Minister of the Czech Republic (first and second Babiš cabinets)
description: Appointed after ANO won the October 2017 election. His single-party minority cabinet lost a confidence vote on 16 January 2018 (117–78) and continued in caretaker capacity; he was reappointed on 6 June 2018 and formed a minority coalition with ČSSD, which won confidence on 12 July 2018 with Communist support. His term covered the COVID-19 pandemic and the 2021 expulsion of Russian diplomats over the 2014 Vrbětice explosions. He left office after the 2021 election, when Petr Fiala's cabinet was appointed on 17 December 2021.

role: Prime Minister of the Czech Republic (third Babiš cabinet)
description: Appointed by President Petr Pavel on 9 December 2025 after publicly committing to give up Agrofert; his ANO–SPD–Motoristé sobě cabinet was appointed on 15 December 2025, approved its programme statement on 5 January 2026 and won a confidence vote 108–91 on 15 January 2026. It survived opposition no-confidence motions on 4 February 2026 (84 for, 99 against) and 1 October 2026 (83 for, 94 against).
